source_text:
Notata sunt etiam commercia haereticorum cum magis quam pluribus, cum circulatoribus, cum astrologis, cum philosophis, curiositati scilicet deditis. Quaerite et invenietis, ubique meminerunt. Adeo et de genere conversationis qualitas fidei aestimari potest. Doctrinae index disciplina est. Negant deum timendum. Itaque libera sunt illis omnia et soluta. Ubi autem deus non timetur, nisi ubi non est? Ubi deus non est, nec veritas ulla est. Ubi veritas nulla est, merito et talis disciplina est. At ubi deus, ibi metus in deum, qui est initium sapientiae. Ubi metus in deum, ibi gravitas, honesta et diligentia adtonita et cura sollicita et adlectio explorata et communicatio deliberata et promotio emorita et subiectio religiosa et apparitio devota et processio modesta et ecclesia unita et dei omnia.
Proinde haec pressioris apud nos testimonia disciplinae ad probationem veritatis accedunt, a qua divertere nemini expedit qui meminerit futuri iudicii, quo omnes nos necesse est apud Christi tribunal adstare, reddentes rationem inprimis ipsius fidei. Quid ergo dicent qui illam stupraverint adulterio haeretico, virginem traditam a Christo? Credo, allegabunt nihil unquam sibi ab illo vel ab apostolis eius de scaevis et perversis doctrinis futuris pronuntiatum et de cavendis abominandisque praeceptum. Agnoscent suam potius culpam et suorum, qui nos non ante praestruxerunt. Adicient praeterea multa de auctoritate cuiusque doctoris haeretici; illos maxime doctrinae suae fidem confirmasse, mortuos suscitasse, debiles reformasse, futura significasse, uti merito apostoli crederentur. Quasi nec hoc scriptum sit, venturos multos qui etiam virtutes maximas ederent ad fallaciam muniendam corruptae praedicationis. Itaque veniam merebuntur. Si vero memores dominicarum et apostolicarum scripturarum et denuntiationum in fide integra steterint, credo, de venia periclitabuntur, respondente domino: Praenuntiaveram plane futuros fallaciae magistros in meo nomine et prophetarum et apostolorum etiam, et discentibus meis eadem ad vos praedicare mandaveram; scilicet cum vos non crederetis. Semel evangelium et eiusdem regulae doctrinam apostolis meis delegaveram; libuit mihi postea aliqua inde mutare. Resurrectionem promiseram, etiam carnis; sed recogitavi, ne implere non possem. Natum me ostenderam ex virgine, sed postea turpe mihi visum est. Patrem dixeram qui solem et pluvias facit; sed alius me pater melior adoptavit. Prohibueram vos aurem accommodare haereticis; sed erravi. Talia capit opinari eos qui exorbitant et fidei veritatis periculum non cavent. Sed nunc quidem generaliter actum est nobis adversus haereses omnes certis et iustis et necessariis praescriptionibus repellendas a conlatione scripturarum. De reliquo, si dei gratia adnuerit, etiam specialiter quibusdam respondebimus. Haec in fide veritatis cum otio perlegentibus pax et gratia dei nostri Iesu Christi in aeternum.
thought_title: Heretics' character and the final judgment
orientation: Tertullian is concluding his treatise by showing that the heretics' conduct reveals their false faith, then imagining their defense at the last judgment and answering it with the Lord's own words.
pass_a_gloss: Also the dealings of heretics have been noted with very many magicians, with wandering charlatans, with astrologers, with philosophers, those devoted to curiosity, of course. Seek and you will find, they remembered everywhere. To such a degree also from the manner of their way of life the quality of their faith can be estimated. The index of doctrine is discipline. They deny that God must be feared. Therefore all things are free and loose for them. But where God is not feared, except where he is not? Where God is not, there is no truth either. Where there is no truth, deservedly there is also such a discipline. But where God is, there is fear toward God, which is the beginning of wisdom. Where there is fear toward God, there is seriousness, honorable and attentive diligence and anxious care and tested choosing and deliberate sharing and mature advancement and religious submission and devout attendance and modest procession and a united church and all things of God. Accordingly these testimonies of a stricter discipline among us come near to the proof of truth, from which it is expedient for no one to turn aside who remembers the future judgment, at which it is necessary for all of us to stand before the tribunal of Christ, giving an account first of all of faith itself. What therefore will they say who have defiled her with heretical adultery, the virgin handed over by Christ? I believe they will allege that nothing was ever pronounced to them by him or by his apostles about harmful and perverse doctrines to come and that nothing was commanded about avoiding and abominating them. They will acknowledge rather their own fault and that of their own people, who did not fortify us beforehand. They will add besides many things about the authority of each heretical teacher; that those men especially confirmed the faith of their own doctrine, raised the dead, restored the weak, signified future things, so that deservedly they were believed to be apostles. As if this too were not written, that many would come who would even produce the greatest powers to fortify the deceit of corrupted preaching. Therefore they will deserve pardon. But if, remembering the Lord's and the apostles' writings and denunciations, they have stood in sound faith, I believe they will be in danger concerning pardon, with the Lord answering: I had plainly foretold that teachers of deceit would come in my name and also in the name of the prophets and apostles, and I had commanded my disciples to preach the same things to you; of course, because you would not believe. Once I had delegated the gospel and the doctrine of the same rule to my apostles; it pleased me afterward to change some things from it. I had promised the resurrection, even of the flesh; but I reconsidered, lest I be unable to fulfill it. I had shown myself born from a virgin, but afterward it seemed shameful to me. I had said that the Father is he who makes the sun and the rains; but another better father adopted me. I had forbidden you to lend your ear to heretics; but I erred. Such things do those think who go off course and do not guard against the danger to the truth of faith. But now indeed it has been done by us in a general way against all heresies, to be repelled from the collation of Scriptures by certain and just and necessary legal objections. For the rest, if the grace of God nods assent, we will also answer certain ones specifically. To those reading through these things in the faith of truth with leisure, peace and grace of our God Jesus Christ forever.

lemmas.gloss: fortified beforehand, built up in advance

choices.why: The word means commercial or social intercourse; 'dealings' preserves the sense of regular association without modernizing to 'business'.
Circulatores were itinerant peddlers or mountebanks; 'wandering charlatans' captures both the itinerancy and the fraudulent character.
The glossary requires 'curiosity' for curiositas, the restless desire to seek beyond received faith.
The glossary requires 'discipline' for disciplina, the ordered teaching and way of life of the church.
Stupro means to violate or defile sexually; 'have defiled' preserves the force of the metaphor of the virgin church violated by heretical adultery.
The glossary requires 'legal objection' for praescriptio, the legal bar against heretics using Scripture.

bible_refs.note: initium sapientiae (fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom)
apud Christi tribunal adstare (we shall all stand before the judgment seat of Christ)
venturos multos qui etiam virtutes maximas ederent ad fallaciam muniendam (false christs and false prophets shall show great signs and wonders)

pass_b_english: Their dealings with itinerants, with wandering charlatans, with astrologers, with philosophers—all people devoted to curiosity—have also been noted. Everywhere they remember, “Seek and you will find” (Matthew 7:7). So the quality of their faith can be judged even from their way of life. Discipline is the index of doctrine. They deny that God must be feared. Therefore everything is free and unbound for them. But where is God not feared, except where He is not? Where God is not, there is no truth either. Where there is no truth, such discipline is deserved. But where God is, there is fear of God, which is the beginning of wisdom (Psalm 111:10). Where there is fear of God, there is seriousness, honest and attentive diligence, anxious care, tested recruitment, deliberate fellowship, mature promotion, religious submission, devout attendance, modest procession, a united church, and all things of God.

These stricter testimonies of discipline among us therefore support the proof of truth, from which it benefits no one to turn aside who remembers the future judgment, when we must all stand before the tribunal of Christ, giving an account first of all of faith itself (Romans 14:10). What then will they say who have defiled her with heretical adultery—the virgin handed over by Christ? I believe they will plead that nothing was ever foretold to them by Him or by His apostles about crooked and perverse doctrines to come, and no command given to avoid and abhor them. They will acknowledge instead their own fault and that of their own people, who did not fortify us beforehand. They will add many things about the authority of each heretical teacher: that those men especially confirmed faith in their doctrine, raised the dead, restored the weak, foretold the future, so that they were rightly believed to be apostles. As if this were not written: that many would come who would even perform the greatest wonders to strengthen the deception of corrupted preaching (Matthew 24:24). So they will deserve pardon.

But if they have stood in sound faith, remembering the Lord’s and the apostles’ writings and warnings, I believe they will be in danger of losing pardon, when the Lord answers: “I had clearly foretold that teachers of deception would come in My name, even in the name of the prophets and apostles, and I had commanded My disciples to preach the same things to you—since you would not believe. Once I had entrusted the gospel and the doctrine of the same rule to My apostles; later it pleased Me to change some things. I had promised the resurrection, even of the flesh; but I reconsidered, in case I could not fulfill it. I had shown Myself born of a virgin; but afterward it seemed shameful to Me. I had called the One who makes the sun and the rains Father; but another, better father adopted Me. I had forbidden you to lend your ear to heretics; but I was wrong.” Such are the things those people are forced to imagine who wander off course and do not guard against danger to the truth of faith.

For now, we have acted generally against all heresies, with certain, just, and necessary legal objections to keep them from any debate over the Scriptures. For the rest, if God’s grace permits, we will also answer certain ones specifically. To those who read these things in the faith of truth with leisure: peace and grace of our God Jesus Christ forever.

problems.quote: I believe they will be in danger of pardon, when the Lord answers
problems.why: Latin means 'they will be in danger OF PARDON' i.e. risk losing it; English implies danger from pardon.
problems.fix: I believe they will be in danger of pardon, when the Lord answers on their behalf
problems.ruling: Latin 'de venia periclitabuntur' means they risk losing pardon; English suggests danger from pardon.

problems.why: Latin mentions 'circulatoribus' (itinerants/wanderers), not magicians; the English adds a category not present.
problems.fix: Replace “magicians” with “itinerants” or “wandering merchants” to match the source.
problems.ruling: Source 'circulatoribus' means itinerants/charlatans, not 'magicians'; adding 'magicians' misleads readers with a category absent from the Latin.

edits.old: I believe they will be in danger of pardon, when the Lord answers
edits.new: I believe they will be in danger of losing pardon, when the Lord answers

edits.old: Their dealings with magicians, with wandering charlatans
edits.new: Their dealings with itinerants, with wandering charlatans

fixed: Changed 'in danger of pardon' to 'in danger of losing pardon' to clarify the Latin 'de venia periclitabuntur' (risk concerning pardon).
Changed 'magicians' to 'itinerants' to match 'circulatoribus' (wandering charlatans/itinerants), removing the added category of magicians.

last_rejected.quote: But if they have stood in sound faith, remembering the Lord's and the apostles' writings and warnings,
last_rejected.source_quote: Si vero memores dominicarum et apostolicarum scripturarum et denuntiationum in fide integra steterint,
last_rejected.why: Source says 'in fide integra' = 'in complete/whole faith'; English renders 'sound faith,' which is within range but loses 'integra.' Also 'denuntiationum' = 'warnings/declarations' is adequate.
last_rejected.fix: But if they have stood in complete faith, remembering the Lord's and the apostles' writings and warnings,
last_rejected.ruling: ‘in fide integra’ rendered as ‘sound faith’; nuance of ‘whole’ not lost, acceptable translation

last_rejected.quote: I had called the One who makes the sun and the rains Father; but another, better father adopted Me.
last_rejected.source_quote: Patrem dixeram qui solem et pluvias facit; sed alius me pater melior adoptavit.
last_rejected.why: Source says 'I had called [Him] Father who makes sun and rain' — i.e., I had called God Father. English 'I had called the One who makes... Father' reverses agency: it makes the weather-maker the object called 'Father' rather than the speaker naming the Father.
last_rejected.fix: I had called Father the One who makes the sun and the rains; but another, better father adopted Me.
last_rejected.ruling: Latin ‘Patrem dixeram qui solem et pluvias facit’ = ‘I called the one who makes sun and rain Father’; English matches

last_rejected.why: The source does not cite Romans 14:10; the citation is an unwarranted addition.
last_rejected.ruling: Source 'reddentes rationem' echoes Romans 14:10; parenthetical reference is standard scholarly annotation, not a meaning change.
